description: A West Coast style voice: an oscillator, a wavefolding overtone branch, a cycling slope generator, a contour envelope and a low pass gate at the output

params.text: Sets the octave in nine steps from -4 to +4; at 0 the oscillator plays C4
Tunes the oscillator over -7 to +7 semitones
Moves the overtone branch through even harmonics, then odd harmonics, and above seven tenths of its travel into ring modulation of the triangle by the Slope
Folds the overtone wave, adding reflections as it is raised
Sets how long the Slope takes to rise, before TIME scales it
Sets how long the Slope takes to fall, before TIME scales it
Scales the Slope rise and fall times together over a forty to one range
Bends the Slope rise and fall between logarithmic and exponential; moving away from centre also shortens both times, by up to 55%
Switches the Slope between one shot and free running; it comes up free running
Sets the attack time of the Contour envelope
Sets the level the Contour holds while its gate is high; at zero a trigger gives a plain attack and decay
Sets the Contour decay and release time
Bends the Contour from linear towards exponential and shortens all of its stages, by up to 65%
Crossfades the output between the plain triangle and the folded overtone branch
Switches the overtone branch into the output; with it off the voice is the plain triangle. It comes up on
Sets the depth of the linear FM taken from the FM input; at zero there is no frequency modulation
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, setting the depth of the modulation reaching MULTIPLY
Holds the low pass gate open so the voice sounds without any gate patched; it comes up off

inputs.text: Volt-per-octave pitch, added to the OCTAVE and FINE knobs
AC-coupled linear frequency modulation of the oscillator, scaled by FM AMT
Offsets OVERTONE, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets MULTIPLY through MLT AMT, 8V covering the knob's full travel; with nothing patched here the Slope is used instead
A rising edge above 1V starts the Slope; an edge arriving during the rise stage is ignored
A rising edge above 1V starts the Slope while TRIG is unpatched, and the voltage here gates the Contour while CTR is unpatched
Shifts the Slope rise and fall times together: each volt halves them, each negative volt doubles them
Shifts the Contour decay and release time: each volt halves it, each negative volt doubles it
Gates the Contour above 1V, taking over from GATE
Drives the low pass gate in place of the Contour while it is patched; 8V opens the gate fully
Offsets TIMBRE, 5V covering the knob's full travel
Shifts the Contour attack time: each volt halves it, each negative volt doubles it
Offsets SUSTAIN, 8V covering the knob's full travel

outputs.text: The oscillator's triangle wave, 10V peak to peak, taken before the overtone branch
The oscillator's square wave, 10V peak to peak, taken before the overtone branch
A 10V pulse 1ms long at the end of the Slope fall
A 10V pulse 1ms long at the end of the Contour attack
The finished voice, after the low pass gate, saturation and DC blocking, ±5V

notes: LINE OUT stays silent until the low pass gate is opened. Patch a gate or trigger to GATE or CTR, patch DYN, or turn DRONE on
the module is monophonic; every input reads its first channel only

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.3:
±8V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the Slope generator; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±8V.
inputs.4:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the GATE input; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.5:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.

a negative voltage does nothing here.

0 to 8V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the Contour envelope; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 5V.
